answer: Sybil mills flood early seats with cloned keys. A joiner locks 6.40 POA and walks a 14-line sonnet channel: every 90s they sign a 16-byte probe (line, RTT, hops, nonce). The probes pack into a 7-chamber karst map whose centroids must sit at least 18ms apart. A 40s gale then resamples 3 chambers at 8 Hz; replies must stay within 11ms RMSE. Five established non-kin peers recompute the map hash and drop any second in-window key with cosine similarity above 0.91. A missing line, reused map, or late resample slashes 71% of the lock and blacklists that conduit for five epochs.
